English Description: Dense foliage provides shelter for small insects and birds; large leaves contribute leaf litter improving soil organic content.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhaban a ɛyɛ den no ma nkoekoemmoa nketewa ne nnomaa nya ahobammɔ; nhaban akɛse a ɛhwe ase no boa ma asase no nya organic matter pii.
Review Note: Cleaned technical wording; scientific meaning preserved.

English Description: Fruit (red when ripe) eaten by birds aiding seed dispersal; palm crown provides nesting sites for small birds.
Final Twi Description: Sɛ n'aduaba no yɛɛ a, ɛyɛ kɔkɔɔ, na nnomaa di, na ɛboa ma aba no trɛw; dua no atifi ma nnomaa nketewa nya baabi yɛ wɔn bere.

English Description: Produces abundant nectar for bats, hummingbirds, and insects during its single spectacular flowering event.
Final Twi Description: Bere a ɛyɛ nhwiren no, ɛma anantwi anadwo, nnomaa nketewa a wɔnom nhwiren mu nsu, ne nkoekoemmoa nya nhwiren mu nsu pii.
Review Note: Replaced unexplained English “nectar” with a spoken description.

English Description: Nitrogen-fixing root nodules enrich soil; abundant nectar-rich flowers attract bees and butterflies; seed pods consumed by birds.
Final Twi Description: Ne ntini so nkwammoaa a ɛboa ma nitrogen kɔ asase mu no ma asase nya ahoɔden; ne nhwiren a nhwiren mu nsu wom pii twetwe nwoawa ne aboɔpɔnkɔ; nnomaa di aba nsina no.

English Description: Nitrogen-fixing root nodules enrich soil; abundant fragrant flowers attract bees and butterflies; seed pods consumed by birds.
Final Twi Description: Ne ntini so nkwammoaa a ɛboa ma nitrogen kɔ asase mu no ma asase nya ahoɔden; ne nhwiren a ɛyɛ huam twetwe nwoawa ne aboɔpɔnkɔ; nnomaa di aba nsina no.

English Description: Native West African species; flowers attract pollinators; fruit consumed by birds; provides habitat for forest insects and small vertebrates in secondary vegetation.
Final Twi Description: Ɛyɛ afifide a ɛyɛ West Africa de; ne nhwiren twetwe mmoa a wɔboa ma afifide nya aba; nnomaa di n'aduaba; ɛma kwae mu nkoekoemmoa ne mmoa nketewa nya tenabea wɔ kwae a ɛsan nyin mu.

English Description: Flowers provide nectar for sunbirds and bees; naturalised populations support local insect communities.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren ma nnomaa ne nwoawa nya nhwiren mu nsu; afifide a anya ne ho wɔ mpɔtam hɔ no boa mpɔtam hɔ nkoekoemmoa.

English Description: Dense foliage provides ground-level habitat for insects; flowers attract small bees and flies.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhaban a ɛyɛ den no ma nkoekoemmoa nya tenabea wɔ asase ho; ne nhwiren twetwe nwoawa nketewa ne nwansena.

English Description: Flowers provide abundant nectar for bees and butterflies; cashew apple fruit feeds birds, bats, and mammals.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren ma nwoawa ne aboɔpɔnkɔ nya nhwiren mu nsu pii; ne cashew apple ma nnomaa, anantwi anadwo ne mmoa di.
Review Note: Kept familiar “cashew apple” rather than inventing a local botanical term.

English Description: Distinctive tiered architecture provides nesting sites for birds; seeds eaten by some bird species.
Final Twi Description: Ne mman a wɔahyehyɛ no afam-afam no ma nnomaa nya baabi yɛ wɔn bere; nnomaa bi nso di ne aba.

English Description: Dense canopy shelters birds and insects; flowers provide nectar for bees; leaf litter enriches soil with nitrogen-containing compounds.
Final Twi Description: Ne dua atifi a ɛyɛ den no bɔ nnomaa ne nkoekoemmoa ho ban; ne nhwiren ma nwoawa nya nhwiren mu nsu; nhaban a ɛhwe ase no ma asase nya nneɛma a nitrogen wom.

English Description: Dense clumps provide nesting and roosting habitat for birds; bamboo thickets support small mammals and insects; watershed protection in riparian zones.
Final Twi Description: Bamboo akuw a ɛyɛ den no ma nnomaa nya baabi yɛ wɔn bere na wɔhome; bamboo kwae nketewa no boa mmoa nketewa ne nkoekoemmoa; ɛboa bɔ nsu kwan ho ban wɔ asubɔnten ho.

English Description: Flowers produce abundant nectar for bees; fruit consumed by birds and bats after natural opening; important native food tree in the Guinean forest zone.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren ma nwoawa nya nhwiren mu nsu pii; sɛ n'aduaba bue ankasa a, nnomaa ne anantwi anadwo di; ɛyɛ aduan dua a ɛho hia wɔ Guinea kwae mpɔtam.

English Description: Dense foliage provides insect shelter; small flowers attract small bees; compact habit supports ground-level insect communities.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhaban a ɛyɛ den no bɔ nkoekoemmoa ho ban; nhwiren nketewa no twetwe nwoawa nketewa; ne nyin a ɛyɛ tiawa no boa nkoekoemmoa a wɔwɔ asase ho.

English Description: Fleshy red fruit is a major food source for fruit bats and birds; plays a documented role in bat seed dispersal at UENR campus; pioneer species that rapidly colonises disturbed areas.
Final Twi Description: N'aduaba kɔkɔɔ a ɛyɛ nam no yɛ aduan titiriw ma anantwi anadwo ne nnomaa; wɔahu wɔ UENR campus sɛ ɛboa anantwi anadwo ma wɔtrɛw aba; ɛyɛ afifide a edi kan nya baabi wɔ asase a asɛe so.

English Description: Minimal wildlife support; mainly ornamental; grown for foliage colour.
Final Twi Description: Ɛboa wuram mmoa kakraa bi; wɔdua no titiriw sɛ afɛfɛde, na wɔpɛ no esiane ne nhaban kɔla nti.

English Description: Flowers attract monarch butterflies and other pollinators; an important larval host plant for several butterfly species in Ghana.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren twetwe monarch aboɔpɔnkɔ ne mmoa a wɔboa ma afifide nya aba; ɛyɛ afifide a aboɔpɔnkɔ ahorow pii wɔ Ghana de wɔn mma nyin so.

English Description: Clusters of black fruit are an important food item for birds; flowers attract moths and other nocturnal pollinators.
Final Twi Description: N'aduaba tuntum akuw yɛ aduan a ɛho hia ma nnomaa; ne nhwiren twetwe anadwo ntontom ne mmoa afoforo a wɔboa ma afifide nya aba.

English Description: Large showy flowers attract hummingbirds and butterflies; provides dense groundcover for insects and small animals.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren akɛse a ɛyɛ fɛ twetwe nnomaa nketewa a wɔnom nhwiren mu nsu ne aboɔpɔnkɔ; ne nhaban a ɛkata asase so no ma nkoekoemmoa ne mmoa nketewa nya tenabea.
Review Note: REMOVED accidental UENR Flora test sentence from the old entry.

English Description: Fast-growing pioneer providing rapid canopy cover; flowers attract bees and hawkmoths; fruit feeds birds and bats.
Final Twi Description: Ɛnyin ntɛm na ɛyɛ afifide a edi kan kata asase so; ne nhwiren twetwe nwoawa ne ntontom akɛse; n'aduaba ma nnomaa ne anantwi anadwo di.

English Description: Nitrogen-fixing symbiosis with Frankia soil bacteria enriches poor soils; pioneer on bare, sandy, and degraded land; provides habitat for seed-eating birds.
Final Twi Description: Ne nkabom ne Frankia bacteria a ɛwɔ asase mu no ma asase a ɛyɛ mmɔbɔ nya ahoɔden; ɛdi kan nyin wɔ asase kwa, anhwea ne asase a asɛe so; ɛma nnomaa a wodi aba nya tenabea.

English Description: Fast-growing canopy tree that supports birds and epiphytes; provides significant wildlife habitat.
Final Twi Description: Ɛyɛ dua a ɛnyin ntɛm na ne dua atifi ma nnomaa ne afifide a ɛnyin nnua so nya mmoa; ɛma wuram mmoa nya tenabea a ɛho hia.

English Description: Nocturnal flowers attract moths and bats for pollination; fleshy red-purple fruit consumed by birds, bats, and mammals.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren a ɛbue anadwo twetwe ntontom ne anantwi anadwo ma wɔboa ma ɛnya aba; n'aduaba kɔkɔɔ a ɛyɛ nam no nnomaa, anantwi anadwo ne mmoa di.

English Description: Flowers attract bees and butterflies as important pollinators; fruit consumed by birds aiding seed dispersal.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren twetwe nwoawa ne aboɔpɔnkɔ a wɔboa ma afifide nya aba; nnomaa di n'aduaba na ɛboa ma aba no trɛw.

English Description: Coconuts float and remain viable in seawater for months, enabling natural dispersal across coastlines; flowers attract bees and small insects; fruit consumed by crabs and large mammals.
Final Twi Description: Akutu tumi sensɛn nsuo so na ɛkɔ so nya nkwa wɔ po nsuo mu abosome pii, enti ɛtumi trɛw ankasa wɔ mpoano; ne nhwiren twetwe nwoawa ne nkoekoemmoa nketewa; akutu no ma akɔre ne mmoa akɛse nya aduan.

English Description: Dense foliage provides cover for small insects; bright foliage attracts birds to campus gardens; flowers attract small insects.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhaban a ɛyɛ den no bɔ nkoekoemmoa nketewa ho ban; nhaban kɔla hyerɛn no twetwe nnomaa ba campus turo mu; ne nhwiren twetwe nkoekoemmoa nketewa.

English Description: Flowers attract bees and small insects; fruit eaten by birds; dense leaf base provides shelter for small lizards and insects.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren twetwe nwoawa ne nkoekoemmoa nketewa; nnomaa di n'aduaba; nhaban no ase a ɛyɛ den bɔ akɔre nketewa ne nkoekoemmoa ho ban.

English Description: Flowers provide abundant nectar for sunbirds and butterflies; flower structure attracts large pollinators; umbrella-shaped crown provides habitat for birds.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren ma nnomaa ne aboɔpɔnkɔ nya nhwiren mu nsu pii; ne nhwiren no sɛnea wɔahyehyɛ no twetwe mmoa akɛse a wɔboa ma afifide nya aba; ne dua atifi te sɛ kyɛw ma nnomaa nya tenabea.

English Description: One of the few native West African plants on this list; flowers provide nocturnal nectar for moths; native range includes the broader West African forest zone.
Final Twi Description: Ɛyɛ West Africa afifide kakraa bi mu baako wɔ saa din yi mu; ne nhwiren ma ntontom nya nhwiren mu nsu anadwo; ɛwɔ West Africa kwae mpɔtam a ɛtrɛw mu.

English Description: Flowers attract butterflies and hummingbirds; yellow-orange berries provide food for birds and small mammals.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren twetwe aboɔpɔnkɔ ne nnomaa nketewa a wɔnom nhwiren mu nsu; n'aduaba a ɛyɛ kɔkɔɔ ne borɔdɔma ma nnomaa ne mmoa nketewa di.

English Description: Dense clumping habit provides nesting sites for birds; small fruits consumed by birds and small mammals.
Final Twi Description: Ne nyin a ɛka bom no ma nnomaa nya baabi yɛ wɔn bere; n'aduaba nketewa nnomaa ne mmoa nketewa di.

English Description: Fruit bunches consumed by birds, bats, and primates; the dense frond canopy provides habitat for many forest species; historically a foundational species in West African forest-savannah mosaics.
Final Twi Description: N'aduaba akuw nnomaa, anantwi anadwo ne mmoa a wɔte sɛ mpaninfoɔ di; ne nhaban atifi a ɛyɛ den ma kwae mu mmoa ahorow pii nya tenabea; efi tete no ɛyɛ afifide titiriw wɔ West Africa kwae ne savanna afrafra mu.
Review Note: Avoided the ambiguous English “primates” with a descriptive phrase.

English Description: Massive canopy tree providing extensive wildlife habitat; nitrogen-fixing; large ear-shaped pods consumed by birds and mammals.
Final Twi Description: Ne dua atifi kɛse no ma wuram mmoa nya tenabea pii; ɛboa ma nitrogen kɔ asase mu; n'aba nsina akɛse a ɛte sɛ aso no nnomaa ne mmoa di.

English Description: Flowers produce abundant nectar attracting bees and birds in some species; allelopathic compounds in leaves suppress native understorey vegetation around the tree base.
Final Twi Description: Nhwiren no ma nhwiren mu nsu pii na ɛtwetwe nwoawa ne nnomaa wɔ ahorow bi mu; nneɛma bi a ɛwɔ nhaban mu si afifide a ɛyɛ kurom a ɛwɔ dua no ase kwan.
Review Note: Preserved allelopathic effect without inventing a technical Twi term.

English Description: Year-round flower-like bracts attract butterflies and small insects for nectar; provides continuous ornamental colour.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren te sɛ nhwiren a ɛkɔ so afe mu nyinaa no twetwe aboɔpɔnkɔ ne nkoekoemmoa nketewa ma wɔnya nhwiren mu nsu; ɛma afɛfɛde kɔla kɔ so afe mu nyinaa.

English Description: Figs provide food for birds, bats, and fruit-eating mammals; dense canopy provides year-round wildlife habitat; fig-wasp mutualism pollination system.
Final Twi Description: Ne borɔdɔma te sɛ n'aduaba ma nnomaa, anantwi anadwo ne mmoa a wodi n'aduaba nya aduan; ne dua atifi a ɛyɛ den ma wuram mmoa nya tenabea afe mu nyinaa; nkabom a ɛda fig ne wasp ntam no boa ma ɛnya aba.

English Description: Keystone fig species; figs provide critical food for birds, bats, and primates; documented in UENR campus bat dispersal study (6.6% of bat-dispersed seeds, Agyei-Ohemeng et al. 2016); pioneer in secondary forest regeneration.
Final Twi Description: Ɛyɛ fig afifide titiriw; ne aduaba yɛ aduan a ɛho hia ma nnomaa, anantwi anadwo ne mmoa a wɔte sɛ mpaninfoɔ; UENR campus nhwehwɛmu kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ 6.6% wɔ aba a anantwi anadwo trɛw mu (Agyei-Ohemeng et al. 2016); ɛdi kan boa kwae a ɛsan nyin.
Review Note: Preserved the 6.6% study result and citation.

English Description: Figs are a keystone food resource for birds, bats, and fruit-eating mammals; aerial roots create complex microhabitats; fig-wasp mutualism is one of the most evolved pollination systems in the plant kingdom.
Final Twi Description: Ne aduaba yɛ aduan titiriw ma nnomaa, anantwi anadwo ne mmoa a wodi n'aduaba; ntini a ɛsian fi mman mu no yɛ tenabea nketewa ahorow; nkabom a ɛda fig ne wasp ntam no yɛ akwan a afifide de boa ma ɛnya aba a anya nkɔso kɛse wɔ afifide ahenni mu.

English Description: Flowering stalk provides nectar for bats and large insects; produces abundant bulbils (plantlets) after flowering for vegetative dispersal.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren dua ma anantwi anadwo ne nkoekoemmoa akɛse nya nhwiren mu nsu; sɛ ɛyɛ nhwiren wie a, ɛyɛ bulbils, anaa afifide nketewa, pii a ɛboa ma ɛtrɛw.
Review Note: Kept “bulbils” with explanation rather than inventing a term.

English Description: Nitrogen-fixing root nodules enrich soil; flowers attract bees and butterflies during dry season when few plants flower; pollarded branches mulch soil.
Final Twi Description: Ne ntini so nkwammoaa a ɛboa ma nitrogen kɔ asase mu no ma asase nya ahoɔden; wɔ ɔpɛ bere a afifide kakraa bi yɛ nhwiren no, ne nhwiren twetwe nwoawa ne aboɔpɔnkɔ; mman a wɔatwa no kata asase so na ɛboa ma asase yɛ fɛ.

English Description: Fast-growing pioneer tree that supports birds and insects; flowers attract bees before leaf emergence; fallen leaves enrich soil rapidly.
Final Twi Description: Ɛyɛ dua a ɛnyin ntɛm na ɛboa nnomaa ne nkoekoemmoa; ne nhwiren twetwe nwoawa ansa na nhaban afi; nhaban a ɛhwe ase no ma asase nya ahoɔden ntɛm.

English Description: Documented in UENR bat sanctuary (9.3% of all individuals per Owusu-Prempeh et al. 2018); seed pods provide food for birds and bats; woody climbing habit contributes to secondary forest structure.
Final Twi Description: Wɔakyerɛw ne ho wɔ UENR bat sanctuary sɛ ɛyɛ nnua no 9.3% (sɛnea Owusu-Prempeh et al. 2018 kyerɛ); aba nsina no ma nnomaa ne anantwi anadwo nya aduan; ne nyin a ɛforo nnua no boa kwae a ɛsan nyin no nhyehyɛe.

English Description: Large trumpet flowers attract sunbirds, butterflies, and bees; one of the most important ornamental nectar sources for campus pollinators.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren akɛse a ɛte sɛ torobɛntɔ twetwe nnomaa, aboɔpɔnkɔ ne nwoawa; ɛyɛ afɛfɛde afifide a ɛma nkoekoemmoa a wɔboa ma afifide nya aba wɔ campus nya nhwiren mu nsu no mu baako a ɛho hia paa.

English Description: Tubular flowers are major nectar source for sunbirds, butterflies, and bees; dense foliage provides shelter for small birds and insects.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren a ɛte sɛ kotoku no yɛ nhwiren mu nsu fibea titiriw ma nnomaa, aboɔpɔnkɔ ne nwoawa; ne nhaban a ɛyɛ den bɔ nnomaa nketewa ne nkoekoemmoa ho ban.

English Description: Flowers attract bees and butterflies; fast-growing pioneer that colonises degraded land rapidly.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren twetwe nwoawa ne aboɔpɔnkɔ; ɛyɛ afifide a ɛnyin ntɛm na ɛdi kan kɔ asase a asɛe so.

English Description: Flowers provide abundant nectar for bees and butterflies during the rainy season peak; semi-deciduous habit creates seasonal leaf litter enriching soil.
Final Twi Description: Bere a osu bere no du ne mpɔtam no, ne nhwiren ma nwoawa ne aboɔpɔnkɔ nya nhwiren mu nsu pii; nhaban no hwe ase wɔ mmere bi mu na ɛboa ma asase nya ahoɔden.

English Description: Nitrogen-fixing root nodules enrich soil; fast-growing pioneer that rapidly colonises disturbed ground; reported nitrogen fixation rates up to 500 kg N/ha/year in optimal conditions.
Final Twi Description: Ne ntini so nkwammoaa a ɛboa ma nitrogen kɔ asase mu no ma asase nya ahoɔden; ɛnyin ntɛm na ɛdi kan kɔ asase a asɛe so; wɔabɔ amanneɛ sɛ sɛ tebea yɛ papa a ɛkyekye nitrogen kodu 500 kg N/ha afe biara.

English Description: Fruit feeds birds and fruit bats; canopy shelters campus wildlife.
Final Twi Description: N'aduaba ma nnomaa ne anantwi anadwo di; ne dua atifi bɔ campus wuram mmoa ho ban.

English Description: Fast-growing pioneer that stabilises bare soil; root zone supports diverse soil microbiome; one of the most drought-hardy staple crops globally.
Final Twi Description: Ɛnyin ntɛm na ɛboa ma asase kwa gyina pintinn; ne ntini mpɔtam boa asase mu mmoa nketewa ahorow; ɛyɛ aduan nnɔbae a etumi gyina ɔpɛ ano paa wɔ wiase.

English Description: Flowers attract small bees; sprawling pioneer that colonises disturbed ground; nitrogen-fixing root nodules.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren twetwe nwoawa nketewa; ɛtrɛw fam na ɛdi kan kɔ asase a asɛe so; ne ntini so nkwammoaa boa ma nitrogen kɔ asase mu.

English Description: Tall columnar form provides vertical structure in campus ecosystems; birds and small insects use canopy for nesting and roosting.
Final Twi Description: Ne tenten a ɛte sɛ dua a ne mu yɛ teateaa no ma campus afifide ne mmoa mpɔtam nya nhyehyɛe a ɛforo soro; nnomaa ne nkoekoemmoa nketewa de ne dua atifi yɛ wɔn bere na wɔhome.

English Description: Flowers rich in nectar attract bees and butterflies; fast-growing pioneer that provides rapid canopy cover.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren a nhwiren mu nsu wom pii twetwe nwoawa ne aboɔpɔnkɔ; ɛnyin ntɛm na ɛkata asase so ntɛm.

English Description: Leaves and decaying pseudo-stems form microhabitats for insects and soil fauna; flower nectar attracts birds and bats.
Final Twi Description: Nhaban ne dua ntam a ɛporɔw no yɛ tenabea nketewa ma nkoekoemmoa ne asase mu mmoa; nhwiren mu nsu twetwe nnomaa ne anantwi anadwo.

English Description: Flowers attract butterflies and bees despite the plant’s toxicity; provides dense evergreen screening.
Final Twi Description: Ɛwom sɛ afifide no yɛ awuduru de, ne nhwiren twetwe aboɔpɔnkɔ ne nwoawa; ne nhaban a ɛyɛ den na ɛyɛ ahabammono bere nyinaa kata ade so.

English Description: Dominant species in UENR bat sanctuary (19.4% of all individuals per Owusu-Prempeh et al. 2018); flowers attract sunbirds and bees; fast-growing pioneer in secondary forest succession.
Final Twi Description: Ɛyɛ afifide a ɛdɔɔso paa wɔ UENR bat sanctuary, na ɛyɛ nnua no 19.4% (sɛnea Owusu-Prempeh et al. 2018 kyerɛ); ne nhwiren twetwe nnomaa ne nwoawa; ɛnyin ntɛm na ɛdi kan wɔ kwae a ɛsan nyin mu.

English Description: Flowers attract bees for pollination; large fleshy fruit historically dispersed by now-extinct megafauna; today dispersed by humans.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren twetwe nwoawa ma wɔboa ma ɛnya aba; tete no, mmoa akɛse a wɔn ase atɔre na wɔtrɛw n'aduaba a ɛyɛ nam no; nnɛ nnipa na wɔtrɛw no.

English Description: Dense evergreen foliage provides year-round shelter for small birds; seeds eaten by some bird species.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhaban a ɛyɛ den na ɛyɛ ahabammono bere nyinaa bɔ nnomaa nketewa ho ban afe mu nyinaa; nnomaa bi di ne aba.

English Description: Fragrant flowers attract moths and butterflies for pollination; everblooming habit provides a consistent year-round nectar source.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren a ɛyɛ huam twetwe ntontom ne aboɔpɔnkɔ ma wɔboa ma ɛnya aba; ɛyɛ nhwiren afe mu nyinaa na ɛma nhwiren mu nsu ba daa.

English Description: Small bees and flies pollinate the inconspicuous flowers; dark purple-black drupes eaten by birds when produced.
Final Twi Description: Nwoawa nketewa ne nwansena boa ma nhwiren a ɛnyɛ fɛ kɛse no nya aba; sɛ n'aduaba tuntum a ɛyɛ kɔkɔɔ-tuntum ba a, nnomaa di.

English Description: Flowers provide abundant nectar for bees; wide spreading canopy provides habitat for birds; nitrogen-fixing root nodules enrich soil.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren ma nwoawa nya nhwiren mu nsu pii; ne dua atifi a ɛtrɛw ma nnomaa nya tenabea; ne ntini so nkwammoaa boa ma nitrogen kɔ asase mu.

English Description: Fast-growing pioneer colonizer of disturbed soils; seeds dispersed explosively when pods dry; provides rapid cover for bare ground.
Final Twi Description: Ɛnyin ntɛm na ɛdi kan kɔ asase a asɛe so; sɛ aba nsina no wu na ɛyow a, ɛma aba no tu fi mu gu ntɛm; ɛkata asase kwa so ntɛm.

English Description: Flowers provide nectar for bees and butterflies during the dry season; documented in UENR bat sanctuary (Owusu-Prempeh et al. 2018), supporting campus wildlife diversity.
Final Twi Description: Ɔpɛ bere mu no, ne nhwiren ma nwoawa ne aboɔpɔnkɔ nya nhwiren mu nsu; wɔahu no wɔ UENR bat sanctuary (Owusu-Prempeh et al. 2018), na ɛboa ma campus wuram mmoa ahorow dɔɔso.

English Description: Flowers attract bees; fruit consumed by birds aiding seed dispersal; pioneer coloniser of disturbed ground.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren twetwe nwoawa; nnomaa di n'aduaba na ɛboa ma aba trɛw; ɛdi kan kɔ asase a asɛe so.

English Description: Large showy flowers provide abundant nectar for sunbirds, hornbills, and butterflies; water collecting in ampule-shaped flower buds is used by tree frogs and insects. CAUTION: nectar toxic to some bee species.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren akɛse a ɛyɛ fɛ ma nnomaa, nnomaa akɛse ne aboɔpɔnkɔ nya nhwiren mu nsu pii; nsuo a ɛboaboa ano wɔ nhwiren aba a ɛte sɛ toa nketewa mu no tree frogs ne nkoekoemmoa de di dwuma. ANSƐE: nhwiren mu nsu no yɛ awuduru ma nwoawa ahorow bi.
Review Note: Kept the caution prominent; retained “tree frogs” because no safe local equivalent was established.

English Description: Flowers attract small bees and butterflies; forms dense mats that exclude native groundcover species. Classified by IUCN as one of the world’s 100 worst invasive alien species.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren twetwe nwoawa nketewa ne aboɔpɔnkɔ; ɛyɛ ntama a ɛyɛ den kata asase so na ɛma afifide a ɛyɛ kurom ntumi nyin. IUCN akyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ wiase afifide amannɔne a ɛtrɛw bɔne no 100 no mu baako.

English Description: Cream pom-pom flowers attract bees and butterflies; fruit consumed by birds and bats aiding seed dispersal.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren a ɛyɛ cream na ɛte sɛ pom-pom twetwe nwoawa ne aboɔpɔnkɔ; nnomaa ne anantwi anadwo di n'aduaba na ɛboa ma aba trɛw.

English Description: Attracts bees and butterflies with its flowers; dense foliage provides shelter for small birds.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren twetwe nwoawa ne aboɔpɔnkɔ; ne nhaban a ɛyɛ den bɔ nnomaa nketewa ho ban.

English Description: Provides nesting sites for birds and insects; teak plantations in Ghana's Brong-Ahafo support soil biodiversity and act as wildlife corridors.
Final Twi Description: Ɛma nnomaa ne nkoekoemmoa nya baabi yɛ wɔn bere; teak plantations wɔ Ghana Brong-Ahafo boa asase mu mmoa ahorow na ɛyɛ akwan a wuram mmoa fa so.

English Description: Fruit consumed by birds, bats, and mammals aiding dispersal; dense tiered canopy provides layered wildlife habitat.
Final Twi Description: Nnomaa, anantwi anadwo ne mmoa di n'aduaba na ɛboa ma aba no trɛw; ne dua atifi a ɛyɛ afam-afam ma wuram mmoa nya tenabea ahorow.

English Description: Distinctive horizontal tiered branching provides nesting sites for birds; provides structured shade below each canopy layer.
Final Twi Description: Ne mman a ɛyɛ afam-afam na ɛtrɛw kɔ nkyɛn no ma nnomaa nya baabi yɛ wɔn bere; nhaban atifi biara ase ma sunsuma a wɔahyehyɛ.

English Description: Native canopy tree that supports birds, bats, and insects; flowers attract pollinators; fruit consumed by birds and bats.
Final Twi Description: Ɛyɛ kurom dua a ne dua atifi boa nnomaa, anantwi anadwo ne nkoekoemmoa; ne nhwiren twetwe mmoa a wɔboa ma afifide nya aba; nnomaa ne anantwi anadwo di n'aduaba.

English Description: Low-growing groundcover protects soil surface from erosion; flowers attract small bees.
Final Twi Description: Ɛnyin fam na ɛkata asase so, na ɛbɔ asase ani ho ban fi nsuo a ɛkɔfa dɔteɛ; ne nhwiren twetwe nwoawa nketewa.

English Description: Forms dense low groundcover mats; minimal direct wildlife support; compact habit suppresses weeds effectively.
Final Twi Description: Ɛyɛ ntama a ɛyɛ den kata asase so fam; ɛboa wuram mmoa kakraa bi pɛ; ne nyin a ɛyɛ tiawa si nwura kwan yiye.

English Description: Flowers attract bees and butterflies; salt-tolerant habit supports coastal vegetation belts; leaves provide food for some butterfly caterpillars.
Final Twi Description: Ne nhwiren twetwe nwoawa ne aboɔpɔnkɔ; etumi gyina nkyene ano na ɛboa mpoano afifide; nhaban no ma aboɔpɔnkɔ mma bi nya aduan.

English Description: Small canopy tree of secondary forest margins; flowers attract pollinators; fruit consumed by birds and bats supporting seed dispersal.
Final Twi Description: Ɛyɛ dua ketewa a ɛwɔ kwae a ɛsan nyin ano; ne nhwiren twetwe mmoa a wɔboa ma afifide nya aba; nnomaa ne anantwi anadwo di n'aduaba na ɛboa ma aba trɛw.

English Description: Pollen feeds a wide range of insects; dry stalks provide shelter for small animals and insects during the dry season.
Final Twi Description: Ne pollen ma nkoekoemmoa ahorow pii nya aduan; bere a ɛyɛ ɔpɛ no, dua a ayow no bɔ mmoa nketewa ne nkoekoemmoa ho ban.
